topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the themes of cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the tumor microenvironment alongside the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Drivers in Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pre-malignant tissues evolve into cancer through the selective growth advantage of successive genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how tissue stem cells and progenitor hierarchies influence cancer initiation and propagation in leukemia and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Tumor Outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how external promoters, inflammatory signaling, and stromal dependencies provide permissive conditions for mutant cell expansion and established tumor maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental Technologies for Mapping Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial profiling tools used to reconstruct the evolutionary history and cellular interactions of tumors.

topics.label: Integrated Model of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture by reviewing how mutational burden, epigenetic plasticity, cell of origin, and microenvironmental conditions intersect to drive malignancy.

topics.label: Closing Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the subsequent lecture on cancer therapy.
